searchText: Regarding our proposition to create an eth2.0-clients organization that would host clients related stuff like common build script and chat apps to debug libp2p, was there any reactions on call on Thursday? https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-pm/issues/85#issuecomment-533089773 <@570268431522201601> https://youtu.be/pEdqjXO6euY?t=926 if you want to hear Danny share your update. No notable reactions, call was very short, mostly due to recent interop lock-in and less researchers on call. **cem_ozer** What kinds of strategies do people use when aggregating attestations? It seems to me that it is not so easy to notice one attestation is a duplicate of another, for example, lets say I have an attestation A with validator 1 and 3 in the aggregation_bits and their aggregated signature, and an Attestation B with with validator only validator 1. How do people notice that the attestation B can be disregarded since attestation A is a superset of it? **shahankhatch** Since attestations come from a partition of validators, i.e., disjoint subgroups, there is a requirement to ensure that the partition is correct. Even with millions of aggregations, verifying a partition's correctness is possible on a small machine. Handel's approach is to structure the validators into a 'binary' tree structure. **shahankhatch** In other words, it does require knowing the graph structure of validators and their aggregations (if any). **shahankhatch** In the worst case, it is linear complexity, the optimal is log(n). **shahankhatch** It also means that peer communication of attestations requires some structure, which I am looking into as part of Handel's integration into Artemis (via jvm-libp2p).
